subject.title: feat(nodes): continue Claude catalog sessions on paired nodes via streaming CLI agent runs

question: Should paired-node catalog continuation remain a dedicated admin-only Anthropic catalog operation, or should OpenClaw deliberately expose a new generic plugin API for streaming node agent runs?
rationale: The branch currently straddles both designs: it publishes generic invocability metadata while rejecting generic invocation, and it creates a privileged node session binding through a write-scoped method. The permanent API and authorization boundary require maintainer intent rather than an automated patch assumption.

options.title: Dedicated admin-only continuation
options.body: Keep the Claude runner private to the catalog flow, remove it from generic `invocableCommands`, and require `operator.admin` before creating the node binding.

options.title: Design a generic runner API
options.body: Pause this landing and define a documented, authorization-aware streaming node-agent API that plugins can actually invoke and upgrade safely.

options.title: Retain write-scoped continuation
options.body: Explicitly accept write-scoped node binding and document why it differs from the existing admin-only session-targeting contract.

recommendation.title: Dedicated admin-only continuation
recommendation.body: Keep the Claude runner private to the catalog flow, remove it from generic `invocableCommands`, and require `operator.admin` before creating the node binding.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged current-main work owns the adjacent catalog continuation UX and they are the strongest available routing candidate for the intended product boundary.
